title: The 'snake attack' rescue is a set-up

scenes.headline: Snake grabs monkey. Human saves it. Staged.
The fight was arranged
scenes.body: Investigators found clips where animals were put together so someone could 'save' one.

scenes.headline: Often the same animals, again and again
scenes.body: Welfare groups report animals being put in danger repeatedly to film more 'rescues'.

scenes.headline: Banned on YouTube. Still uploaded.
scenes.body: Moderators told reporters that review of these videos is slow and inconsistent.

scenes.headline: What we post instead
scenes.body: Wild behaviour, credited footage, named places. No set-ups, ever.

caption:
If the camera was rolling before the 'attack', it wasn't an accident.

One documented example: a python coiled around a gibbon until a person 'discovered' them. Report these videos instead of sharing them.

Source: National Geographic (2021); SMACC 'Spot the Scam' (2024). Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: AVOID format: anti-pattern explainer on the predator-attack-then-rescue trope. Wild CC photos are labelled as wild and shown separately (never paired), so we don't recreate the genre.
